questions.title: What is the difference between localStorage and sessionStorage?
questions.answer: localStorage persists data across browser sessions until it is removed. sessionStorage stores data for a particular origin and browser tab session. Both expose synchronous key-value APIs and store strings.
questions.underTheHood: The browser maintains storage areas associated with origins. sessionStorage is additionally partitioned by top-level browsing context.
pitfalls: Sensitive credentials should not be placed in Web Storage.
followUps: How do cookies differ from localStorage?

questions.title: What are cookies?
questions.answer: Cookies are small pieces of data associated with websites. They are commonly used for sessions and preferences and can be automatically included in HTTP requests according to their attributes.
questions.underTheHood: Browsers store cookies with attributes controlling scope, expiration and transmission. Attributes such as Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite affect security and request behavior.
pitfalls: HttpOnly cookies cannot be read through document.cookie.
Cookies can be included in network requests.
Cookie security depends on appropriate attributes.
followUps: What is the difference between cookies and localStorage?
